subject.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk

question: After the stale-acquisition defect is fixed, should this PR’s tombstone-retention model become canonical for deletion and reset, including owned files under an external trajectory directory?
rationale: The mechanical defect can be repaired automatically, but retaining sensitive tool-call records and extending retention cleanup into operator-configured directories is an intentional data-lifecycle and security-boundary choice.

options.title: Adopt unified retention
options.body: Fix stale same-owner acquisition, approve this branch as canonical, and supersede the overlapping reset implementation.

options.title: Narrow to deletion
options.body: Keep only deletion orphan cleanup and writer retirement, deferring reset retention and external-directory aging to separate owner-approved work.

options.title: Prefer the reset PR
options.body: Use the narrower reset implementation and request a separate bounded deletion and writer-lifecycle fix.

recommendation.title: Adopt unified retention
recommendation.body: Fix stale same-owner acquisition, approve this branch as canonical, and supersede the overlapping reset implementation.
